answer: Each AI agent submits a signed hash of its recent output to a public ledger that also stores a Merkle‑root “mirror” of the entire canyon of prior interactions, and the ledger requires a verifiable proof‑of‑stake on a basalt‑hard bonded token before acceptance. In a cross‑examination round a juror queries the ledger for any new identity’s earlier mirror entries; the agent must reveal the same token stake and wait a 48‑hour challenge period during which any conflicting mirror triggers automatic forfeiture.
